fields.meta_title: Report Automation With Checks Before It Sends | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe a report you rebuild by hand, and Emergent builds report automation that pulls the figures and checks them before each send.
fields.h1: Build Report Automation That Checks the Numbers First
fields.hero_description: Build report automation that pulls figures from your tools, tests them against your rules, and sends each report on time.
fields.features_heading: What Runs Behind Every Scheduled Report
fields.features_subheading: The app gathers, tests, and delivers each report, and a person sees it first only when a number calls for it.
fields.feature_1:
Numbers pulled from every source

Connects to your ad accounts, CRM, store, and accounting software through their APIs. Each run starts from the figures those systems hold that morning, not from last week's export.
fields.feature_2:
Checks against last period and budget

Compares each figure with the prior period or the budget before anything goes out. When a number moves past a threshold you set, the report waits and its owner sees which line moved.
fields.feature_3:
Sign-off only where it matters

Holds client and board reports for a named reviewer, who adds context and approves the send. Routine internal reports go out on their schedule without anyone opening them first.
fields.feature_4:
Delivery to inboxes and Slack channels

Emails each finished report to its list, posts a summary to the Slack channel that acts on it, or publishes it behind a client login. Every send is logged with the version sent.
fields.feature_5:
Dashboards that admit when data is stale

Refreshes each tile on its own schedule and labels any tile whose source failed to sync with the time of its last good update. Nobody mistakes an old figure for today's number.
fields.feature_6:
A reporting app you can take with you

Exports the full code, with its queries and delivery schedules, to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Every past run stays in a database you own, ready for any BI tool to read.

fields.usecase_heading: Reports Teams Stop Building by Hand
fields.tab_content_1:
A bad month gets a note before the client sees it

When the month closes, the app pulls Larch Dental's ad spend from Google Ads and Meta, plus its leads from HubSpot. That comes to $18,400 for 230 leads, or $80.00 a lead against $64.00 last month. Any rise in cost per lead over 20% holds the report until Corinne Vance, the account manager, notes the cause.
fields.tab_content_2:
Budget misses arrive with their explanation

Three business days after close, the app sets last month's actuals from QuickBooks against budget. Two lines missed by more than 10%: software at $22,500 against $18,000, and travel at $10,350 against $9,000. Ravi Sethi and Joanna Pike, who own them, each get a request for a short note. The CFO pack waits for both.
fields.tab_content_3:
Late orders grouped by cause before the shift starts

At 7:00 every morning, the app counts the previous day's orders from Shopify and your warehouse system, then posts to #ops-daily. Yesterday 1,196 orders shipped and 14 left late: nine packed after the 4:00 PM carrier cutoff, and five waited on stock. The shift lead starts with the cutoff misses.
fields.tab_content_4:
A failed sync is labeled stale, not left blank

The leadership dashboard refreshes at 6:00. MRR came in from Stripe at $286,400 and cash from QuickBooks at $612,000. HubSpot needed reauthorizing. Instead of going blank, the pipeline tile kept yesterday's $940,000 under a stale label. Iris Navarro, who owns that connection, got a direct message to reconnect.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up report automation for a recurring report, with checks that run before every scheduled send.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the report that takes longest
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List every number and its source
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Collect the last three finished reports
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide what should stop a send
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a report someone rebuilds by hand every week or month. Note who builds it, how long it takes, and who reads it. A report with a fixed layout and a fixed audience makes the best first candidate; one-off analysis does not.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down each figure in the report and the system it comes from: spend from the ad account, revenue from accounting, orders from the store. Mark any figure someone calculates in a spreadsheet, and copy out the formula they use.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Gather the three most recent versions exactly as they went out. They show the layout readers expect and give you known-good numbers to test against. Emergent builds the first version of the app from your description and these examples.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write down the checks a careful analyst makes before sending: cost per lead up by a fifth, a budget line off by more than 10%, a source that did not refresh. Name the person who receives each report the app holds back.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Connect sources and set the schedule
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect each system through its API and set when the report runs, such as 7:00 each weekday or the third business day after close. Run it once by hand and compare every figure with the last report your team sent.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run both versions for two cycles
fields.howto_step_6_des: Keep building the report by hand for two cycles while the automated version runs beside it. Where the numbers differ, find out which side is wrong and describe the fix to Emergent in a prompt. Stop once two runs match.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Point the email list or Slack channel at the automated report and retire the manual copy. Leave the hold rules on. Each month, look at which reports were held, and adjust any threshold that fires too often or never fires.

plan.angle: The top 10 are BI and RPA vendors defining automated reporting and listing tools, plus Reddit threads asking how to get a recurring report off someone's desk. This page shows four reports running end to end: an agency's monthly client report held for a note when cost per lead jumps, a month-end budget report that asks line owners to explain misses before it goes to the CFO, a 7:00 AM shipping report posted to Slack with late orders grouped by cause, and a leadership dashboard that labels a figure stale when a connection fails instead of leaving the tile blank. Definitions, tools, AI, accuracy, client and financial reporting are answered in the FAQ.
tab_stories: When the month closes the app builds a dental client's ad report from three sources, and because cost per lead rose 25% against a 20% rule, it waits for the account manager's note before it emails the client.

Three business days after close the app compares last month's actuals from QuickBooks with budget, and the two lines that missed by more than 10% go to their owners for a short explanation before the pack reaches the CFO.
At 7:00 every morning the app counts the previous day's orders from the store and the warehouse system and posts a Slack summary: 1,196 shipped, 14 late, nine of them packed after the carrier cutoff.

When the HubSpot connection needs reauthorizing, the leadership dashboard keeps yesterday's pipeline figure under a stale label beside fresh MRR and cash, and the analyst gets a direct message to reconnect.
